title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' Grothendieck studies pairs of elements (ρ, σ) in GL2 and SL2. The 'cas modulaire' is ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] (order 6, characteristic polynomial x²−x+1) and σ = [[0,-1],[1,0]] (order 4, characteristic polynomial x²+1). These are the standard generators of SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. He is computing the structure of an auxiliary algebraic group SG*_{ρ,σ}(0). This group is a symmetry or stabiliser group of the configuration. On the previous page it was embedded in T_ρ × N'_σ, where T_ρ is the centraliser torus of ρ and N'_σ is a normaliser-type extension of the centraliser T_σ. It is cut out by the relations det b = ε' det a with ε'² = 1. The map (u,a,b) ↦ (ε(b), det b/det a) to μ2×μ2 is surjective because the determinant maps δ_ρ, δ_σ are epimorphisms.

On this page:
(23) An exact sequence 1 → SG*°_{ρ,σ}(0) → SG*_{ρ,σ}(0) → μ2×μ2 → 1. Its kernel SG*° is identified with the subgroup scheme of T_ρ×T_σ given by (24) det a = det b, i.e. the fibre product T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ over the two determinant maps.
(25), (26) A dévissage 1 → ST*_ρ × ST*_σ → SG*° → G_m → 1, with (a,b) ↦ det a = det b. Here ST* = Ker(det: T → G_m) is the norm-one subgroup of the centraliser.

Remarks on ST*: if ρ (resp. σ) is regular semisimple, T_ρ is a maximal torus (of dimension 2) and ST*_ρ is a one-dimensional torus. In the modular case:
- ST*_ρ is a torus except in characteristic 3, where x²−x+1 = (x+1)² and ρ is −(unipotent). There the centraliser is G_m×G_a and the norm-one part is μ2×G_a.
- Likewise ST*_σ is a torus except in characteristic 2.
- The crossed-out conclusion reads, in substance: away from characteristics 2 and 3, SG*° is a torus of dimension 3 (dimension 4 − 1).

He then announces the next step. To get SG* from SG*° and the semidirect-product decomposition, one must make explicit the action on Λ0. The next page shows this action factors through δ_σ.

Purpose: a structural description (torus by finite group, with bad primes 2 and 3) of the automorphism or stabiliser group scheme relevant to solving the loop equations for the modular-group generators over a general base.
errors: Minor notational inconsistency: SG*°, SG°* and SG° are used interchangeably. In the last line he writes G^{°*}_{ρ,σ(0)} where SG^{°*} is meant.
The page refers to 'la décomposition (22) en produit semi-direct', but (22) is the map to μ2×μ2. The intended reference is the split extension (23); a splitting is presumably given via N'_σ.

The claims that ST*_ρ and ST*_σ are tori must exclude characteristics 3 and 2 respectively, as the text apparently does. In those characteristics the groups are non-reductive (μ2×G_a type), which is consistent.

ideas.what: Fibre product of the centraliser tori over the determinant, T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ, with its dévissage into norm-one tori and G_m
ideas.modern_name: Norm-one tori, fibre products of tori, centralisers of regular elements in GL2
ideas.where_published: general torus theory in SGA3; this specific computation unpublished

ideas.what: Bad characteristics 2 and 3 for the modular generators: the centraliser of the order-6 (resp. order-4) element ceases to be a torus in char 3 (resp. 2)
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of SL2(Z) torsion elements mod 2 and 3; non-semisimple reduction

ideas.what: Structure of the stabiliser group scheme as an extension of μ2×μ2 by a 3-dimensional torus, as a tool for the loop-equation analysis
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism group schemes of representations of the modular group / GT-type equations
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche context (unpublished manuscript notes)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine structural computation: an extension of a finite 2-group by a torus, plus elementary observations on bad characteristics 2 and 3. It is correct and standard, with no new result or connection beyond the general (already known) context of the 'équation des lacets' notes.
transcription_corrections: 'ST*_ρ est un tore [?] en car. 3' should most likely read 'est un tore sauf en car. 3'; likewise for ST*_σ 'sauf en car. 2'.
The crossed-out passage likely reads 'Donc, sauf en car 2, 3, SG°*_{ρ,σ(0)} est un tore de dim 3'.
'k-scindé [?]' is uncertain; the sense is that ρ is regular semisimple (k-split), so that T_ρ is a maximal torus of dimension 2.
In the second line SG°_{ρ,σ(0)} should carry the * as in (23): SG*°.
Under (25) the annotation should read '(a,b) ↦ det a = det b' (the 'Ker' and the first 'det' are crossed out).
